subject: general
question: Which of the following phenomena CANNOT be explained using the universal law of gravitation?

options.text: Motion of planets around the Sun
Motion of the moon around the earth

solution:
The correct answer is __**Firing of a gun**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The universal law of gravitation primarily deals with the gravitational attraction between masses.
 
• It explains the motion of celestial bodies like planets around the Sun and the moon around the Earth.
 
• Tides are influenced by the gravitational pull of the moon and the Sun on Earth's water bodies.
 
• Firing of a gun involves the forces of combustion, pressure, and projectile motion, not gravitational attraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Universal Law of Gravitation**

 
 
• Formulated by Sir Isaac Newton, it states that every mass attracts every other mass in the universe with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• This law explains various phenomena including planetary orbits, free-fall, and the behavior of tides.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion**
 
 
• Describes the motion of an object thrown or projected into the air, subject to only the acceleration of gravity.
 
• Firing a gun results in projectile motion, where the bullet follows a curved trajectory due to gravity and initial velocity imparted by the gunpowder explosion.
 
 
 
• **Combustion in Firearms**
 
 
• When a gun is fired, the gunpowder combusts and rapidly converts into gas, creating high pressure.
 
• This pressure propels the bullet forward and out of the barrel.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Forces**
 
 
• Caused by the gravitational interaction between the Earth, Moon, and Sun.
 
• Tides result from the difference in gravitational pull on different parts of the Earth's surface.
